guideSummary.surfnerd: Baishawan is a north-facing, white sand beach break with easy access from Taipei on the train and bus. It is often flat through summer, and in winter it turns cold and windy with little power or shape, which is why it tends to draw kiteboarders, windsurfers and hang gliders as much as surfers. If you want a better wave nearby, the high-tide reefbreak called Wedding Plaza sits a little further east, and closer to town at Danshuei, Shalun Beach can throw up a messy, rolling wave for beginners.
guideSummary.surfForecast: Paishawan Beach in - is a reasonably exposed beach break that has reasonably consistent surf. Winter is the favoured time of year for surfing here. The best wind direction is from the east southeast. Windswells are much more common than groundswells and the ideal wave angle is from the northeast. The beach breaks offer lefts and rights. Rarely crowded here. Watch out for rocks.

guideSummary.surfnerd: Jin Shan, also known as Green Bay or Golden Mountain, is a sandy beach break that throws both lefts and rights. The peaks spread out between the boulders at the north end and the jetty in the middle, so there is room to find your own section. It is usually fairly average and easygoing, but it can turn good on the backside of a typhoon.

guideSummary.surfnerd: Bashien Dong is a long, left-hand boulder pointbreak tucked below Eight Fairy Cave, and it shows off just how much power Taiwanese surf can carry. On its day it lines up great walling lefts, with soft shoulders out the back giving way to the odd short peeler on the rocky inside before a heavy shorepound. Keep an eye on the rivermouth, which can throw up intense rips and pushes some rights off to the north.

guideSummary.surfnerd: Jialeshui, also written Jia le Shui, is one of the main spots in south Taiwan and one of the most dependable. Its bankability means there's usually something to ride in most swells. Lefthanders skirt a rocky reef in the shadow of the long headland, peeling lazily for a fair distance, while a rivermouth peak in the middle of the beach works a shifting sandbar.

guideSummary.surfForecast: Nanwan Beach (South Bay) in South Taiwan is a reasonably exposed beach and reef break that has fairly consistent surf. The optimum conditions for surfing are during the cyclone season. Ideal winds are from the north northwest. Windswells are much more typical than groudswells and the ideal wave direction is from the southeast. The beach breaks favour lefts and there is right hand reef break too. Often Crowded. Take care of the strong rips here.
